Description: Student independently works the problem (by hand, with a calculator, or step-by-step on their own) in order to verify the AI's response after receiving it. Solving the problem oneself ALONG or USING the AI's provided steps still counts as A1 when the student produces their own work; add A2 only if they also describe reading through the AI's reasoning as a separate check.
Do NOT apply when: The student only reads or follows the AI's printed steps without producing their own solution (-> A2). The student explicitly solved FIRST and uses AI as the checker (-> A5).
Distinguish from: A2 (reading vs. re-deriving); A5 (direction of verification)
Example responses: "Try the question on my own" • "I redo it by hand" • "Do the problem and the math myself." • "I usually check by doing the math" • "I solve the questions myself using the steps it gives me."

Description: Student reads through, follows, or walks through the AI's reasoning/derivation to look for errors, without independently re-deriving the solution.
Do NOT apply when: The student re-derives the solution themselves (-> A1). The student only judges whether the final answer seems reasonable (-> A3 or D1). The student solves the problem themselves using the AI's steps, producing their own work (-> A1).
Example responses: "I go through the steps and see if they look right" • "Walking through the process they gave" • "I go through its th[inking]"

Description: Student describes an active plausibility judgment performed as a routine part of their workflow: common sense, physical intuition, units, magnitudes, directions.
Do NOT apply when: Checking is described as conditional, rare, or triggered only by suspicion (-> D1). No judgment of any kind is described (-> D2). No plausibility criterion is named: a bare 'I make sure it's correct based on my knowledge' describes judging the solution content (-> A2, or D1 if conditional), not a distinct sanity check.
Distinguish from: D1 (routine judgment vs. conditional/passive checking); A4; A2 (a named criterion such as units, magnitude, direction, or physical sense vs. general correctness judgment)
Example responses: "usual checks of units, magnitude, and direction" • "I try to think if the numbers make sense in the context of the [problem]"

Description: Student checks whether the AI correctly interpreted the problem inputs: the diagram or figure, geometry/positions, given values, or what is being asked.
Do NOT apply when: The check concerns the AI's reasoning or arithmetic rather than its reading of the problem inputs (-> A2 or A1).
Example responses: "check to see if it read the diagram correctly" • "I usually do a sanity check and check positions first because AI [misreads diagrams]"

Code: Solves First, Uses AI as Checker
Description: Student's workflow is the reverse of A1: they complete the problem on their own FIRST, and the AI's role is to check the student's work.
Do NOT apply when: The student solves in response to an AI answer in order to check the AI (-> A1), or the order is ambiguous (default -> A1).
Example responses: "I never copy directly -- I do everything out by hand and use AI to check my work rather than check the AI." • "Usua[lly I solve first]"

Description: Student checks the AI response against course-provided resources: lecture notes/slides, the course textbook, posted solutions or answer keys.
Do NOT apply when: The resource is generic and not course-provided, e.g., Google or YouTube (-> B5). The student consults a person rather than materials (-> B2/B3).
Example responses: "Compare with posted solutions from professors" • "answer key" • "I'll check the answer keys posted." • "See if it c[orresponds with lecture notes]"

Description: Student verifies the AI response (or the discrepancy between their answer and the AI's) by consulting course staff: professor, TA, LA, office hours.
Do NOT apply when: The people consulted are classmates or friends (-> B3).
Example responses: "I usually go office hours to check with TA and stick with my answers." • "if I was not sure if the AI generated ans[wer was right I would ask the professor]"

Description: Student verifies by comparing answers or discussing the AI response with classmates, friends, or groupmates.
Do NOT apply when: The person consulted is course staff (-> B2).
Example responses: "Check it with my classmate and my own work" • "I check my answers with others to see if what they did was the same."

Description: Student runs the same question through one or more DIFFERENT AI tools/models (or re-runs the same tool for a fresh, independent response) and compares.
Do NOT apply when: The student pushes back within the same conversation with the same AI (-> C1a/C1b).
Distinguish from: C1a/C1b (independent second source vs. same-conversation intervention)
Example responses: "I would ask multiple tools to do the same problem and compare answers" • "Cross validate across models" • "re-run t[he same question]"

Description: Student uses open-web resources that are NOT course-provided: Google searches, YouTube solution videos, online databases.
Do NOT apply when: The resource is course-provided (-> B1). The 'online' resource is another AI model (-> B4).
Example responses: "Look it up online to see if it makes sense" • "I place the answer on Google first to see if there is a match"

Description: Student asserts to the AI that something is (or may be) wrong: points out a suspected mistake, supplies a correction, or pushes back on a specific step.
Do NOT apply when: The student asks for a recheck without asserting an error (-> C1b). The student asks the AI to explain or justify its reasoning (-> C1c). The follow-up is generic ('I prompt further', 'I ask about it') without asserting an error or requesting a redo (-> C1c).
Distinguish from: C1b; C1c (assertion vs. request vs. probe)
Example responses: "I will then, typically, prompt the AI thing with 'I think this should be 50 feet, not 40'" • "I've had many multi m[essage exchanges correcting it]"

Description: Student asks the AI to double-check, verify, recheck, or redo its own work, without asserting that a specific error exists.
Do NOT apply when: The student names a suspected error (-> C1a). The student switches to a different AI model (-> B4).
Example responses: "Ask if it can double check." • "If I get a different answer, I ask for it to recheck." • "have the AI check through [its work]"

Description: Student asks follow-up questions whose FUNCTION is to expose errors or test the AI's understanding, without directly asserting an error. Default code for generic, unspecified further prompting after a suspected issue ('if I find discontinuity, I prompt further') when the response does not state that an error was asserted (C1a) or a redo requested (C1b).
Do NOT apply when: The follow-up is purely to learn or understand the concept for the student's own sake, with no verification function.
Example responses: "Ask it to explain its answer in detail" • "I try to ask sub-questions to create manageable chunks for the AI… and I [check each chunk]"

Description: Student asks the AI to provide sources or citations and then independently checks those specific sources for accuracy.
Do NOT apply when: The student searches online for corroboration without reference to AI-provided citations (-> B5).
Example responses: "I usually have an AI provide me with sources which I check for accuracy." • "I make sure to cross-reference with th[e sources it gives]"

Description: Student describes checking that is conditional, rare, or passive: they check only when an answer seems off or surprising.
Do NOT apply when: The judgment is described as a routine part of the workflow (-> A3). No checking of any kind is described (-> D2).
Distinguish from: A3 (conditional/passive vs. routine); D2 (some checking vs. none)
Example responses: "Normally I only check if I think the answer doesn't align with what I've learned" • "I check… when the numbers seem [off]"

Description: Student explicitly states they do not check AI responses at all, with no conditional or minimal checking described.
Do NOT apply when: Any checking behavior is described, however minimal or conditional (-> D1 or A3). The student doesn't check because they don't use AI (-> E1).
Example responses: "I dont lmao" • "I do not check if the concepts the AI tool explains are correct." • "I usually don't."

Description: Student states they do not use AI tools, or have not used AI in this course, so the verification question does not apply. STANDALONE: never combine with any other code.
Do NOT apply when: The student uses AI but skips verification (-> D1/D2).
Example responses: "I don't use AI" • "Haven't used AI in this course" • "I do not use AI." • "I don't use it for mechanics"

Description: Response is blank, 'N/A', 'yes/no' with no elaboration, 'don't know yet', nonsensical, or otherwise contains no identifiable verification behavior. STANDALONE: never combine with any other code.
Do NOT apply when: Any other code can be applied, even at low confidence (apply it and flag for review instead of discarding). The response describes how the student uses or adapts AI output (e.g., 'I use the AI methods, not its answers') -- code the described behavior (A/B/C/D codes) instead; describing use is codable content.
